description: The Holistic Electricity Model (HEM) is a National Laboratory of the Rockies (formerly NREL) iterative framework for analysing how structural change in electricity systems affects the whole ecosystem and each stakeholder. Contents: instead of a single central planner, HEM models each stakeholder's behaviour as an optimisation problem or a system of equations in the Julia language and iterates between them; for example a regulator approves retail rates from a pro forma system of equations while an independent power producer makes profit-maximising investment decisions. It is designed to add new stakeholder types, metrics and decision processes, and to apply to multiple jurisdictions, timeframes and technologies. Producer: NLR Energy Systems Analysis, with a technical review committee of stakeholder representatives. Coverage: generic; the first case study looks at distributed photovoltaic adoption in a bulk power system of natural gas and utility-scale PV, examining regulatory structure, retail rate design and DPV compensation. Format and access: the page gives no download link. Licence: not stated on the NLR page. Caveats: availability and documentation outside NLR are not stated. Simulation uses: exploring how rate design, self-supply and decentralisation change utility investment, customer investment and retail rates. Related records: model-reeds and data-openei-utility-rate-database-urdb-us-international-electricity-tariffs.
